title: Obama mocks Trump’s response to Cheesecake Factory jibe. ‘They mobilized a whole of government response to that joke!’ – as it happened
text:
From 8h agoObama mocks Trump's response to Cheesecake Factory jibe. 'They mobilized a whole of government response to that joke, not to inflation, but to that joke!'We are still watching simultaneous rallies, for Republicans in Ohio, and for Democrats in Georgia, that have overlapped in interesting ways at times.Minutes ago in Ohio, Donald Trump responded his indignation to his predecessor Barack Obama’s joke that “he’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.”“I paid for it myself. I fixed it, and now it’s more beautiful and in better shape,” Trump said, defending the quality of his renovations to the White House. “President Obama,” he added, was miffed because he is someone “who doesn’t understand cleanliness, who doesn’t understand broken, cracked stone and sidewalk, who doesn’t understand that having asphalt going to your main entrance is not the right thing”.A short time later in Georgia, Obama repeated his jibe and then reflected on the outraged response to his joke.“The guy is building a ballroom that is bigger than the White House. He’s paved over the Rose Garden, put a helicopter pad on the South Lawn, and there is gold everywhere. So much gold,” Obama said. “This is a fact, I’m not making this up. He, the president of the United States, is spending time super-gluing gold medallions to the mantel in the Oval Office. I am not making this up. He is literally doing arts and crafts while we are fighting a war and trying to deal with out-of-control prices.”“I heard the president was not happy when I joked over the weekend that he’s got the white House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” the former president said. “First of all, let me get this on the record: I am the father of two daughters. Do you think, could have survived their childhood without going to the Cheesecake Factory?”“Chucky Cheese and California Pizza Kitchen and the Cheesecake Factory – that was my jam for about a decade,” Obama said.“The interesting thing about how the administration responded to the speech I gave the other day. They did not dispute what I said about them being directly responsible for rising prices. They did not argue with that,” Obama continued. “They did not deny tariffs were contributing to higher costs for families. They didn’t say anything about that. I accused this administration, based on the facts, that they were engaging in unprecedented levels of corruption. They didn’t say anything about that. The president wasn’t even mad about the Saddam Hussein comparison. That part didn’t bother him, but he was very upset about the Cheesecake Factory comments. He took great umbrage. He said, I didn’t understand the work of the artisans in the White House.”“It’s all crazy, but this was the really crazy part,” Obama added. “They mobilized a whole of government response to that joke - not to inflation, but to that joke.”“The White House even called the secretary of the treasury – this is the man who is in charge of the economy, the person who’s supposed to be figuring out how to make your life more affordable, the guy who’s supposed to be figuring out how to lower inflation and reduce interest rates. They told him he should hold a press conference in front of the Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said, to laughter from the crowd.Cris Seda Chabrier contributed reporting.Key events6h agoClosing summary7h agoTrump again defends Ramaswamy ad featuring Amy Acton's mother, who sided with husband accused of raping her pre-teen daughter7h ago'We got to keep reality TV on Bravo," Obama says, 'We don’t need it in the White House'8h agoObama mocks Trump's response to Cheesecake Factory jibe. Here are the latest developments:

 Barack Obama mocked the Trump administration’s response to his joke that Donald Trump has added so much gold to the Oval Office that he’s “got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.” After Trump again defended his renovations, Obama said “They mobilized a whole of government response to that joke - not to inflation, but to that joke.”

 A federal judge declined to order California election officials to segregate ballots from people the Trump administration claimed were non-citizens, rebuffing a legally thin request from the justice department that appeared designed to cast doubt over the results of the midterms.

 Jason Turkish, who is engaged to Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens, appeared at a campaign event for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan and told reporters he was voting for the Republican, not Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who narrowly defeated Stevens in the Democratic primary.

 A heckler disrupted Trump’s speech in Ohio by shouting “Trump went on the Jeffrey Epstein plane!” The president then congratulated himself for banning his friend of at least 17 years from his beach club. “I threw Jeffrey Epstein out of a club like 20 years ago, because I thought he was a whack job,” Trump said.

Sam LevineA federal judge declined to order California election officials to segregate ballots from people the Trump administration claimed were non-citizens, rebuffing a legally thin request from the justice department that appeared designed to cast doubt over the results of the midterms.The ruling from US district judge David Carter, nominated to the federal bench by Bill Clinton, comes about two weeks after the justice department delivered a USB drive to election officials in Los Angeles and Sacramento that it said contained the names of 20,000 non-citizens on the state’s voter rolls. There are more than 23 million registered voters in California and non-citizen voting is extremely rare.“This case is about the right of every American citizen to vote in a free and fair election,” Carter wrote in his Wednesday evening ruling. “Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch.”“In bringing this lawsuit, the Executive would have this Court believe that it reigns as a sole sovereign,” Carter continued. “But California and its people are sovereign, too.”The justice department gave officials just 48 hours to review the list and said it would sue the state if officials did not sequester ballots from those whose citizenship it could not confirm. The department refused to provide more details about its methodology and Los Angeles officials found preliminary indicators the list was inaccurate. The justice department then sued California on 15 October to try and force the state to sequester the ballots and verify citizenship.Trump again defends Ramaswamy ad featuring Amy Acton's mother, who sided with husband accused of raping her pre-teen daughterSpeaking in Ohio on Wednesday, Donald Trump doubled down on his support of an attack ad released by the Republican candidate for governor, Vivek Ramaswamy, which features criticism of his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton, from her estranged mother, who lost custody of her daughter at age 12, when her second husband was accused of raping her daughter.Trump, who was asked last Friday by Monica Alba of NBC News, “do the sexual abuse allegations mean nothing to you?” again ignored that aspect of the story and complained that Ramaswamy was being treated “unfairly” by the media.Donald Trump speaks during a campaign rally at the Shoemaker Center at Ohio University on 28 October. Photograph: Mark Schiefelbein/AP“The mother said that Amy Acton, the daughter, is a liar, that she’s no good, that she lied about the opponent, how the hell is that his problem?” Trump asked, referrign to Ramaswamy, who was widely criticized by both Republican and Democratic officials for releasing the ad.“He had the mother of his opponent say that her daughter was a liar,” Trump said. “The fake news criticized him.”The president then argued, as he has before, that if is mother had said something like that about him, and it was used in an ad, no one in the media would have objected and “the press would be getting Pulitzer prizes.” He again refused to acknowledge that his hypothetical excluded the serious sexual abuse allegations Acton’s mother is accused of ignoring.Trump also accused Alaska Democrats of “cheating” for reportedly working to recruit a candidate named Dan Sullivan to be on the ballot in a US Senate race there against the Republican incumbent, Dan Sullivan. The president called for the Democratic candidate Mary Peltola to be prosecuted, but made no mention of what law he thinks she violated.“Nobody can tell the difference. This is voter fraud at the highest level and the Democrat candidate who is involved in the scheme, Mary Peltola, who said she didn’t know anything about it” Trump said, “she should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted, and so should the fake Dan Sullivan.”'We got to keep reality TV on Bravo," Obama says, 'We don’t need it in the White House'Both Donald Trump and Barack Obama have now finished speaking at dueling rallies in Ohio and Georgia.“We need serious people in Washington and state capitals, these are serious times, Obama said near the end of his remarks in Atlanta, in support of the Democratic nominee for governor, Keisha Lance Bottoms and senator Jon Ossoff.“We seem to constantly just tolerate unseriousness. The people who are currently in charge, they’re not doing their homework. They’re not they’re not doing their work. They’re not presenting realistic plans,” Obama said. “These are people who are more interested in performance and flexing and texting and putting people down rather than lifting them up.”“They enjoy insulting and dividing instead of bringing people together to solve problems,” he added. “I know we’re in Atlanta and I want y’all to know Michelle has love for the Real Housewives. But we got to keep reality TV on Bravo. Leave it to the professionals. We don’t need it in the White House. We don’t need it in the governor’s mansion. We need people like John and Keisha in there.”In contrast, Trump wound up his remarks by having his supporters watch television – specifically a CNN clip from a month ago that showed he remains very popular with people who describe themselves as “Maga Republicans”. The president did not mention that this clip was taken from a much longer segment that detailed just how unpopular he is with everyone else, including non-Maga Republicans.Obama mocks Trump's response to Cheesecake Factory jibe.
